Subject: Post-call notes — EchoHealth performance baseline and clarifying asks

Thanks for the walkthrough today — helpful conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can lock down the acceptance criteria for the hosted eval: 

Summary of incumbent (our current provider):
- Typical steady-state: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 1.05s (observed across our production mix)
- Streaming sessions: average concurrency per region ~ 120, bursts up to ~520 for short windows (10–30s)
- End-to-end measurement includes client-side pre-processing and our gateway (~120ms median) — we care about client-to-client perceived latency.

Clarifying asks for Redwood: 
1) How do you define p95 / p99 for hosted? Is it server-processing-only or full e2e (client -> server -> client)?
2) For streaming, what are the concurrency safety limits for the hosted plan versus a Dedicated pool?
3) During a canary you mentioned automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant — how will that impact tail behavior?

Attached: traffic_profile_aug2028.xlsx — contains our region breakdown, session length distribution, and sample traces.

Preferred test window: Aug 28–30 (PST).

Thanks,
Devon

Thanks Devon — great context and thanks for the attachment. Recap and proposed next steps below.

High-level answers:
- Redwood hosted p95/p99: by default we report end-to-end latency measured at the API gateway (client TCP -> final token emitted). For fairness we can harmonize with your gateway measurement if you prefer (we can add a 3rd-party probe to measure client-to-client).
- Concurrency: hosted (shared) is safe up to ~150 steady concurrency per region for streaming with our current slotting; beyond that we recommend a Dedicated pool or a temporary burst reservation.
- Fallbacks: model variant fallback is functionally graceful — it trades off token throughput and slightly increased token latency on long contexts. We instrument tail quantiles per-request so we can produce p95/p99 breakouts by model variant during the canary.

Proposed acceptance plan (short):
1) Harmonize measurement (we will run probes simultaneous with your traces so we measure the same client path).
2) Controlled canary (48–72h) with: 
   - Traffic shaping to mimic your concurrency envelope (steady + bursts),
   - Canary run split: 70% served by hosted fast-path model, 30% routed to fallback variants to validate graceful degradation,
   - Collect p50/p95/p99, error rate, and time-to-first-byte for streaming.
3) Post-canary readout + decision: we produce a report and suggested tuning (batching, prefix caching, or Dedicated sizing).

I'll attach our short tech brief and a template runbook for the canary. Can Camila own scheduling and Rishi own the Dedicated-sizing follow-up?

Next steps:
- Camila to propose two 2-hour windows for the canary (we heard Aug 28–30 from you).
- Hannah (SRE) to share the runbook and minimal measurement probes.
- Rishi to produce a preliminary Dedicated-sizing calc if bursts exceed hosted comfort.

Thanks,

Adding the engineering checklist and measurement plan so everyone has the runes. I'm attaching the runbook snippet and including the specific tests we need to run during the canary.

Measurement approach (we will provide scripts/probes):
- E2E definition: client start -> application-level final token delivered (we will instrument using a small JS probe and a server-side correlation id). This matches EchoHealth's ask for client-perceived latency.
- Key metrics to collect: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99, TTFB for first token on streaming, error-class breakdown, and per-request KV-cache hit rate.
- Trace alignment: please keep your gateway timestamps in the traces so we can correlate with our API timestamps.

Canary test matrix (minimal):
- Baseline phase (6h): steady concurrency 100/session pattern from traffic_profile (validate baseline p95/p99).
- Burst phase (4h): scripted bursts up to 520 concurrent sessions for 10–30s windows every 20 minutes (repeat pattern to exercise autoscaling).
- Degraded-path phase (4h): introduce 30% of requests routed to quantized/fallback variants to observe tail delta.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- p95 end-to-end <= 300ms for normal steady load (matches expected client-side budget + server processing);
- p99 end-to-end <= 1.2s for steady load;
- During bursts, p95 must not exceed 600ms more than 1% of the burst windows;
- Error rate during canary <= 0.2% and no systemic disconnects in streaming.

Instrumentation and artifacts we will deliver:
- Canary-run dashboard (Grafana) with correlations, per-model tail breakdowns, and per-region traces.
- Raw trace package (incumbent_trace_sample.json is useful for alignment).

Attachment: hannah_runbook_snippet.md (text/markdown)

Great — locking in Aug 29 02:00–08:00 UTC for the canary. Quick answers on fallback: 
- Live diversion mechanics: we do not forcefully migrate in-flight streaming sessions between hosting tiers (protocol constraints make seamless handoff for active streams hard).
- Practical fallback pattern: we recommend a staged diversion where new sessions are routed to Dedicated capacity when the autoscaler signals sustained elevated queueing. Existing sessions stay on the current host. We'll script sticky routing so session-affinity is preserved, and sessions created after the cutover use Dedicated.
- Rishi will follow up with a Dedicated-burst sizing calc and an order-of-magnitude cost delta so you can approve temporary reserve capacity if needed.

Action items assigned: 
- Camila: confirm the final canary window and owner contact list by EOD today.
- Hannah: stand up probes and Grafana dashboard; deliver pre-canary sanity run.
- Rishi: Dedicated-sizing calc and an emergency burst-reserve quote.
- Devon: confirm sample traces uploaded and outbound contact for on-call during the window.

I'll schedule a 30-minute post-canary readout for Aug 30. Thanks everyone — looking forward to the run.
